key_insight: MPFlow learns where to open a limited number of Lightning Network channels so a node’s routing capacity, measured by max-flow, increases as much as possible.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical decision tool for liquidity placement in payment networks, helping operators allocate capital to channels that improve throughput under a fixed budget.
method: Model channel opening as budgeted graph optimization: choose k edge additions to maximize s–t max-flow.
Use a message-passing graph policy network trained with PPO and action masking.
Apply a hub-exclusion curriculum so the policy learns capacity-aware placement instead of simply attaching to the highest-degree nodes.
evidence_signal: The method was tested on real Lightning Network snapshots and outperformed strong heuristic baselines across multiple seeds and unseen graphs, with deployment results covering 4,640 channel-open decisions and 267.3 BTC allocated across 30 managed nodes.
watch_item: Performance is tied to the quality and stability of Lightning Network snapshots, so deployment may require careful adaptation to changing network topology and liquidity conditions.
paper_title: MPFlow: Learning Budgeted Max-Flow Optimization on the Lightning Network with Deep Graph Reinforcement Learning
